title: Adding a transcendental variable preserves geometric irreducibility
statement: Let $M\subseteq L\subseteq K$ be a tower of fields [def-pc-field-extension] such that $L/M$ is geometrically irreducible [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. If $x\in K$ is transcendental over $L$, then $L(x)/M(x)$ is geometrically irreducible.

proof.text: Lift the ambient field K to ULift K in universe max u v. The canonical L-algebra equivalence sends x to a transcendental element, hence its constant Fin 1 family is algebraically independent by Mathlib algebraicIndependent_unique_type_iff. Apply the forward implication of [lem-zl-geometric-irreducibility-transcendental] to this singleton. Set.range_const identifies its generated fields with M(up x) and L(up x).

The canonical ULift algebra equivalence restricts to equivalences M(x) ≃ M(up x) and L(x) ≃ L(up x), by IntermediateField.equivMap, adjoin_map and image_singleton. Their square with the two inclusions commutes on underlying elements. To transport geometric irreducibility between the possibly different scheme universes, use [lem-zl-geometric-irreducibility-separable] on both extensions. A separable element maps to a separable element by Mathlib IsSeparable.of_equiv_equiv; the lifted criterion puts it in the lifted base, and injectivity of the equivalence puts the original element in the original base. Apply the criterion backwards. This yields precisely geometric irreducibility of L(x)/M(x).
